note: Five strategies over one ranking. Each adds a single layer to the one before it. #1 is the strategy the Trade Plan follows; change it from the Compare tab and commit this file so both founders see the same pick.
designNote: Every layer here controls risk rather than picking better stocks, because that is what the score does not already do. Filters that repeat the score (MACD, relative strength, above-50-DMA) were tested and dropped — they reject high-scoring names and push the basket deeper down the ranking for no gain. A tempting RSI-85 filter was also dropped: it doubled the backtest at exactly 85 and reversed at 80 and 90, which is a fitted artefact, not a signal.

strategies.name: Core
strategies.blurb: The original plan. Rank the universe, buy the top 7 in equal rupee amounts, hold for the month, stop at 2.5x ATR.
strategies.adds: Baseline — everything else is measured against this.

strategies.name: Equal risk
strategies.blurb: Same seven names, but sized by 1 divided by ATR. A stock that swings 5% a day gets a smaller position than one that swings 2%, so every holding puts about the same rupees at risk.
strategies.adds: Position sizing. Equal money means the wildest name quietly decides your month.

strategies.name: Spread
strategies.blurb: Widens the basket from 7 names to 10 — the three that would otherwise sit on the bench get bought too. Same equal-risk sizing.
strategies.adds: Diversification. One bad name does less damage when it is a tenth of the book instead of a seventh.

strategies.name: Balanced
strategies.blurb: Spread, plus a cap of two names from any one sector. The score ranks companies one at a time and has no idea it just handed you four auto-component stocks.
strategies.adds: Concentration control — the risk a per-stock score structurally cannot see.

strategies.name: Consensus
strategies.blurb: Every stock gets a vote from the four strategies above — a vote means that strategy would hold it. On all four shortlists = full position. On three = half position. Fewer than three = skipped. If fewer than ten names qualify it holds fewer and keeps the rest in cash rather than forcing the basket full.
strategies.adds: Conviction weighting, on top of equal-risk sizing and the sector cap.

primaryNote: Set to Balanced (S4) because it led the 2-year backtest on both return and drawdown. Consensus (S5) had the lowest volatility. Change this from the Compare tab once live tracking has an opinion.
